hero.text: A six-month professional preparatory course for candidates sitting the Primary Elocution Teachers' Diploma examination of the Colombo Association of Language Skills and Dramatic Art.

blocks.title: Who awards this diploma
bullets: The **Primary Elocution Teachers' Diploma is awarded by CALSDA** — the Colombo Association of Language Skills and Dramatic Art — which also sets and conducts the examination.
**RCF Online Academy does not award this diploma.** It conducts a preparatory course for candidates who intend to sit the CALSDA examination.
**RCF Online Academy is not an official representative, agent or branch of CALSDA**, and does not speak for it.
Entry requirements, the syllabus, examination dates and CALSDA's own fees are matters for CALSDA. Please confirm them with CALSDA directly before enrolling.

blocks.heading: What the course is
text: A **six-month professional preparatory course**, conducted online by R. C. Fernando, for candidates who intend to sit the Primary Elocution Teachers' Diploma examination.

It is a teaching course, not an examination. Its purpose is to prepare a candidate to present themselves for the CALSDA examination with the speech work, the reading and the confidence that the examination calls for.

blocks.heading: How the course is taught
blocks.eyebrow: The same method as the rest of the Academy
intro: Speech work improves the way writing does: by being shown, practised with guidance, then performed independently and corrected.

items.title: Clear explanation
text: Each element is explained plainly before it is practised, so a candidate knows what is being asked of them and why.

items.title: Demonstration
text: The teacher models the work aloud. Speech cannot be learnt from a page alone; it has to be heard.

items.title: Guided practice
text: Candidates practise with the teacher listening, and are corrected as they go rather than afterwards.

items.title: Independent performance
text: Candidates present prepared work without support, as they will have to in the examination.

items.title: Individual correction
text: Each candidate is corrected individually. This is the part of the course that does most of the work.

items.title: Regular revision
text: Earlier work is returned to deliberately through the six months, rather than covered once and left.

blocks.heading: This course
intro: Where a day, time, fee or number of places has not been settled, the card says so rather than guessing. The current position is always available on WhatsApp.

blocks.title: What this course does not promise
bullets: **No examination result is promised.** Whether a candidate passes is decided by CALSDA, on the day, on their own work.
**No place in the CALSDA examination is arranged by this course.** Candidates enter the examination through CALSDA themselves.
**No entry requirement is waived.** If CALSDA requires anything of a candidate, this course cannot alter it.

hero.text: A six-month professional preparatory course for candidates sitting the Associate Diploma, the higher elocution diploma examination of the Colombo Association of Language Skills and Dramatic Art.

blocks.title: Who awards this diploma
bullets: The **Associate Diploma is awarded by CALSDA** — the Colombo Association of Language Skills and Dramatic Art — which also sets and conducts the examination.
**RCF Online Academy does not award this diploma.** It conducts a preparatory course for candidates who intend to sit the CALSDA examination.
**RCF Online Academy is not an official representative, agent or branch of CALSDA**, and does not speak for it.
Entry requirements, the syllabus, examination dates and CALSDA's own fees are matters for CALSDA. Please confirm them with CALSDA directly before enrolling.

blocks.heading: What the course is
text: A **six-month professional preparatory course**, conducted online by R. C. Fernando, for candidates who intend to sit the Associate Diploma examination.
The Associate Diploma is the higher of the two elocution diplomas prepared for at the Academy. Candidates should satisfy themselves, with CALSDA, that they are eligible to sit it before enrolling.

blocks.heading: How it differs from the Primary Diploma course
text: Both courses run for six months and are taught the same way: explanation, demonstration, guided practice, independent performance, individual correction and regular revision.

The Associate Diploma course works at a higher level and expects more of a candidate from the outset — more demanding material, longer prepared work, and a greater share of the time spent on independent performance rather than on demonstration.

If you are unsure which of the two suits you, say what you have already done and you will be advised honestly. Being pointed at the right course matters more to us than filling a place in the wrong one.

bullets: **No examination result is promised.** Whether a candidate passes is decided by CALSDA, on the day, on their own work.
**No place in the CALSDA examination is arranged by this course.** Candidates enter the examination through CALSDA themselves.
**No entry requirement is waived.** If CALSDA requires anything of a candidate, this course cannot alter it.

pages.title: Grade 9 Literature
pages.metaTitle: Grade 9 Literature course | RCF Online Academy
pages.description: An online Grade 9 English Literature course at RCF Online Academy: reading poetry, short stories and drama closely, and learning to build an answer rather than retell a story.
pages.keywords: Grade 9 Literature, English Literature class, online literature course, Sri Lanka

hero.text: The year to build the habits that make the Ordinary Level course straightforward: reading closely, finding evidence, and explaining an effect.

blocks.heading: What the course covers
text: Grade 9 is where Literature is either enjoyed or given up on. The course is built to make it the first.
bullets: **Reading a poem** — who is speaking, what changes, and what the words are doing.
**Reading a short story** — where it begins, where it turns, and what the ending leaves open.
**Reading a play** — following it as something watched rather than only read.
**Finding evidence** — going back to the text instead of answering from memory.
**Explaining an effect** — the sentence that turns a description into an answer.
**Writing a paragraph answer** — point, evidence, explanation, effect and link, practised until it is a habit.

blocks.title: Why start at Grade 9
text: Most students who struggle at Ordinary Level are not short of ability. They arrive in Grade 10 having read texts but never having been shown how an answer is built, and then spend two years trying to learn that under examination pressure.
A year spent on the habits first makes the two that follow much easier.

pages.title: Grade 10 Literature
pages.metaTitle: Grade 10 Literature course | RCF Online Academy
pages.description: An online Grade 10 English Literature course at RCF Online Academy: the prescribed texts studied closely, with context and essay answers practised and corrected individually.
pages.keywords: Grade 10 Literature, O/L Literature first year, English Literature class, online course

hero.text: The first year of the Ordinary Level course, taken at a pace that allows the texts to be studied properly rather than covered in a rush.

blocks.heading: What the course covers
bullets: **The prescribed texts**, read whole first and then studied closely, in the same fifteen sections used across this site.
**Context questions** — placing an extract and judging how long an answer should be.
**Essay questions** — reading the question, planning, and building an argument.
**Themes and characters**, expressed as sentences that can be argued rather than lists of words.
**Quotations** — ten per text, chosen because each is useful for more than one question.
**Individual correction** of written answers, with one paragraph rewritten each time.

blocks.title: You will need the prescribed texts
text: Copyrighted literary texts are not reproduced on this website or supplied with the course. Students need their own copies of the prescribed books.
Prescribed texts are set by the examination authority and change from time to time. **Check the current official syllabus for your own examination year.**

pages.title: O/L Literature
pages.metaTitle: O/L Literature course | RCF Online Academy
pages.description: An online O/L English Literature course at RCF Online Academy: prescribed texts, context and essay answers practised under timed conditions, with individual correction.
pages.keywords: O/L Literature class, English Literature tuition, online literature course, Grade 11

hero.text: Examination year. The texts studied in full, answers written under timed conditions, and every piece of work corrected individually.

blocks.heading: What the course covers
bullets: **The prescribed texts**, completed and revised rather than met for the first time.
**Context answers** matched to the marks — short, because context answers should be short.
**Essay answers** planned in five minutes and written to time.
**Answer development** — point, evidence, explanation, effect and link, drilled until automatic.
**Common mistakes** — the errors that recur every year, and each student's own list.
**Past-paper practice**, marked, with one answer rewritten each time.
**Individual correction** of every piece of written work.

blocks.title: You will need the prescribed texts
text: Copyrighted literary texts are not reproduced on this website or supplied with the course. Students need their own copies.
**Confirm the prescribed texts for your own examination year against the current official syllabus.** They change from time to time, and every year some candidates prepare the wrong ones.

pages.title: A/L Literature
pages.metaTitle: A/L Literature course | RCF Online Academy
pages.description: An online A/L English Literature course at RCF Online Academy: close reading, critical appreciation of unseen passages, and well-organised essay answers.
pages.keywords: A/L Literature class, Advanced Level Literature tuition, critical appreciation course

hero.text: Advanced Level Literature taught as a set of abilities to be built: close reading, evidence, effect, argument and essay organisation.

blocks.heading: What the course covers
bullets: **The prescribed texts**, read whole in the first term and then studied closely across the two years.
**Critical appreciation of unseen poems and passages** — one a fortnight, timed, because this skill improves only with repetition.
**Selecting evidence** — going straight to the two or three moments that answer a question.
**Analysing effect** — the sentence most candidates never write, and where the higher marks live.
**Developing an argument** — qualifying, complicating and meeting the strongest objection.
**Critical approaches**, used as questions to ask a text rather than labels to attach to it.
**Examination technique** — choosing questions, dividing time, and the final ten minutes.

blocks.title: Prescribed texts and your own copies
text: Students need their own copies of the prescribed texts. Copyrighted works are not reproduced on this website or supplied with the course.
**Confirm the list for your own examination year against the current official syllabus.** Prescribed texts are revised periodically.
